title: "Examples"
subtitle: "Typst, compiled as this page builds."
description: "Typst figures, tables, equations, and inline expressions compiled to images by the extension, with the options that shape them."
# A ```{typst} block looks like an executable cell to Quarto's engine
# detection, which then selects Jupyter and fails for want of a kernel. The
# extension compiles those blocks itself, so the page needs no engine.
engine: markdown
---

Every figure below is compiled by the Typst binary Quarto ships, as this page is rendered.
The site asks for SVG, so they stay sharp at any zoom:

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-render:
    format: svg
```

## A figure

````markdown
```{typst}
#circle(radius: 1cm, fill: blue)
```
````

```{typst}
#circle(radius: 1cm, fill: blue)
```

## A table

````markdown
```{typst}
#table(
  columns: 3,
  [*Format*], [*Writer*], [*Figures*],
  [HTML], [html], [image],
  [PDF], [latex], [image],
  [Typst], [typst], [native or image],
)
```
````

```{typst}
#table(
  columns: 3,
  [*Format*], [*Writer*], [*Figures*],
  [HTML], [html], [image],
  [PDF], [latex], [image],
  [Typst], [typst], [native or image],
)
```

## An equation

```{typst}
$ integral_0^1 x^2 dif x = 1/3 $
```

## Inline expressions

An inline expression scales to the text around it, so a red word `{typst} #text(red)[hello]` sits in a sentence, and so does a formula `{typst} $ x^2 + y^2 = z^2 $`.

Give it alt text for a reader who cannot see it:

```markdown
The area is `{typst} $pi r^2$`{alt="pi r squared"} for a circle of radius r.
```

Without an `alt` attribute the Typst source is used instead.

::: {.callout-note}
Inline Typst is not available in PowerPoint, since Pandoc cannot put an image inside a run of text there.
Blocks work normally.
:::

## Showing the source

`echo` puts the Typst beside its output, and `code-fold` tucks it away:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| echo: true
//| code-fold: true
#circle(radius: 0.6cm, fill: green)
```
````

```{typst}
//| echo: true
//| code-fold: true
#circle(radius: 0.6cm, fill: green)
```

Per-block options use the comment and pipe form, `//| key: value`, at the top of the block.

## An interaction worth knowing

::: {.callout-caution}
This site does not run the `code-window` filter, unlike the others in this family.

`code-window` claims ```` ```{typst} ```` blocks at `pre-quarto` and rewrites them into decorated code blocks, so `typst-render` never sees them and no figure is produced.
Running both, the blocks come out as ordinary listings with `{typst}` as their filename.
:::

## Source

The repository ships a short, standalone starting point you can copy: [`example.qmd`](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-typst-render/blob/main/example.qmd).

Every release attaches `example-render.tar.gz`, that same file rendered to HTML, Typst, PDF through each of the three LaTeX engines, RevealJS, Beamer, Word, and PowerPoint.
It is on the [latest release](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-typst-render/releases/latest), and is the way to see one source come out as figures in nine outputs.
